01Document · 4 sectionsAI needs context. And boundaries.+

A useful AI integration combines a specific task, relevant information and a way to review the result.

Start with a specific task

Summarising text, classifying a request and proposing a draft are different tasks. Describing the input a function receives and the output the process needs helps determine whether a model adds value.

Also establish when the application should request more information or return the work to a person instead of continuing with an inadequate response.

Provide context deliberately

Context should be relevant to the task and authorised for that use. External information processed by a model is content, not a source of permissions or new instructions for the application.

Integration secrets belong on the server and in its protected configuration. The browser does not need a credential to display the result of an operation.

Validate before acting

If the application expects a particular structure, it must validate that structure and its values before using them. Convincing wording does not guarantee that a response is correct or suitable for taking action.

Operations that change data or affect other people need authorisation controls in the application and, where appropriate, human review. The model does not replace those decisions.

Evaluate with examples from the process

A useful evaluation includes typical inputs, ambiguous cases and situations with missing information. Check both response quality and the system’s ability to recognise when help is needed.

Keeping test examples makes it possible to review the integration when instructions, context or the model change. The goal is to improve the behaviour of the complete solution.

02Document · 4 sectionsIntegration starts with the contract.+

Before the connector or endpoint, questions about data, responsibilities and failures deserve an answer.

Understand the business operation

Start by describing the process: what triggers it, which system owns the data and what the person using it needs. A useful integration preserves that meaning from beginning to end.

A Power Apps application, Power Automate flow and .NET API can take part in the same process. The choice of components depends on their responsibilities and the constraints of the environment.

Make the exchange explicit

The contract describes fields, types, identifiers, optional values and expected responses. It should also clarify how dates are represented and how errors are communicated.

Distinguish a validation failure from an operation that cannot be completed at that moment. That difference lets an interface or automation respond coherently.

Design the error path too

A service can become temporarily unavailable and a request can be repeated. Before adding retries, understand whether repeating the operation might create a duplicate or perform an action twice.

An operation identifier and contextual logging help trace the exchange across systems. Credentials and data that the log does not need should stay out of it.

Test the complete process

Beyond a successful response, review incomplete inputs, missing permissions, unexpected responses and external service failures. Test how the process continues and what the user is told.

Documenting the contract and error-handling decisions makes the integration easier to evolve when one of the systems changes.

03Document · 4 sectionsA good interface starts before JavaScript.+

Content, links and structure first. Interactivity next. Progressive enhancement as a design and development decision.

A foundation people can read

The main content should exist in the document delivered to the browser. A heading, paragraph and link are useful on their own: they do not need to wait for a function to finish running.

On Alejandro’sTech, language routes, projects, experience and notes are generated as HTML. The browser enhances the experience with filters, animations and controls, but the information is already there.

Every control has a job

A link takes you somewhere; a button performs an action. Respecting that difference helps keyboard navigation, assistive technology and familiar browser behaviours work predictably.

Interaction also needs perceptible feedback: which technology is selected, whether an animation is paused or whether an address was copied. That state is part of the interface.

Motion is a layer

Animation can explain a relationship or give an identity character. It should also be possible to stop it. A reduced-motion preference, a hidden tab or an offscreen effect are situations worth handling explicitly.

The home portrait is an HTML image. Smoke and the loader grid are optional decorative layers that can stop; information and links remain available independently of those effects.

Test the foundation and its enhancements

Review the page with and without its enhancements: reading on narrow screens, visible focus, keyboard navigation, link destinations and behaviour when a resource is unavailable.

A useful question is specific: can someone find what they need and take the next action? Visual effects should support that answer.

04Document · 4 sectionsHow this demo works+

Scope, sources and boundaries of the document assistant.

A bounded library

This assistant answers questions about four public documents: Alejandro’sTech’s three original technical notes and this guide. It does not search the internet, access private files or accept document uploads. It is a personal prototype exploring AI integration in software, not a client case study.

Each query is independent. The application keeps no question or answer history. Navigating away or reloading clears the conversation from the screen.

From question to evidence

Lightweight consultation runs in the browser: it matches words and concepts and shows verbatim passages with their sources. It does not write with a model. If you enable optional AI, the device downloads Qwen3.5 and uses the retrieved passages to generate an answer in the page’s language.

The application accompanies the generated paragraph with the source and excerpt used as context. Identifiers, links and passages come from the library; the model does not invent them. If generation fails or does not pass these checks, it shows passages instead and indicates the change. A valid citation helps review the answer, but does not guarantee that its entire interpretation is correct.

When information is missing

If the library provides insufficient evidence, the assistant should acknowledge it. It must not invent sources, professional facts, prices or project outcomes. You can rephrase the question or open the documents to check what they contain.

The demo does not execute actions, change data or send messages to other people. Answers are guidance and require human review before being applied to a real system.

Privacy and availability

Questions and answers are processed on the device and are not sent to an AI service. There are no keys or API usage charges. The optional download of approximately 450 MB retrieves public files from Hugging Face and may keep them in the browser cache; you can delete them from the demo. Conversations are not stored.

Downloadable AI requires WebGPU and sufficient memory. Lightweight consultation remains available when the browser is incompatible, the download is cancelled or the model fails. Leaving the demo releases the model; returning does not automatically start another download or generation.

Library updated on 7 November 2026

An experiment with clear boundaries.

  • Closed library: no internet search or private files.
  • Lightweight consultation from the start; optional downloadable AI.
  • No automatic actions, API charges or query history.
  • Local AI can make mistakes: review its sources and interpretation.

Cookies and privacy

What we store

The at_consent cookie remembers your choice for six months. Optional settings are stored locally for the same period. You can withdraw permission here: those settings will be deleted. Controls still work during your visit if you choose necessary only. If you enable the demo’s optional AI, the browser may store model files; delete them from the demo itself. Questions are not stored.

When you submit the form, your name, email, subject and message pass through Formspree to reach alejandro.dev.sergio@outlook.com. They are used to respond to your enquiry. The provider processes and stores details under its privacy policy. Do not include passwords or sensitive information.
